title: Foreseen, yet free (Avot 3:15)
hook: all is foreseen, yet freedom is given, and the world is judged with goodness
tomorrow: who's keeping the record, and what's written in it?

segments.voice: Yesterday, beloved, and told so: love has to be spoken to reach someone. Today Akiva's hardest line, small enough to fit on a strip of tape.

On a stage floor there are little marks of colored tape. The director put them down weeks ago: you'll stand here, then here. Every actor's feet are foreseen. And still, how you cross from one mark to the next, fast, slow, afraid, laughing, is yours. Akiva's line would fit on one of those strips: hakol tzafui, veharshut netunah. All is foreseen, and permission is given.
screen: `TAPE ON THE STAGE FLOOR.` → `THE MARKS ARE SET.` → `THE WALK IS YOURS.`

segments.voice: Akiva doesn't explain how both can be true. He sets them side by side with an and between them. Tzafui means seen ahead, watched. Reshut means permission, room, freedom to act. Later thinkers worked hard at the knot. Maimonides calls free choice a pillar of the Torah, and says that God's knowing isn't like ours, so we can't picture how it fits with our choosing. Others simply hold both and keep walking. And notice how big and how small the words are. Hakol, all: not some, not only the big moments. Reshut, permission, is given: a gift, not something grabbed. Then Akiva adds two more phrases. The world is judged with goodness, uvetov ha'olam nidon. And all according to the weight of deeds. That isn't a trap. It's a promise: the judging leans kind, and it looks at the whole of a life, not one bad night. So the free part is real, and it adds up. Every step between the tape marks counts.
screen: `ALL IS SEEN AHEAD.` · `AND FREEDOM IS GIVEN.` · `MAIMONIDES: A PILLAR.` · `JUDGED WITH GOODNESS.` · then, large: `FORESEEN, YET FREE.`

segments.voice: Sit with both feet flat and feel exactly where they are, the mark you're on. Choose one small movement, a hand turning over, a slow shift of weight, and before you make it, notice that it hasn't happened yet. Then make it, slowly, and feel that it was yours.
Foreseen. Tzafui in Akiva's Hebrew: seen ahead, and in the very same line, freedom given.
Here's the line: foreseen, yet free, and every step between the marks is yours. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Jews study Avot 3:15 together with Maimonides' laws of repentance, chapter five, where free choice is called a pillar of the Torah.

match.prompt: Akiva's two halves — tap the pairs.

fork.setup: you didn't get the job you wanted, and your aunt says, "it was meant to be." by Akiva's line, what's true?
options: both: it may be foreseen, and what you do next is still free.
nothing you do now matters; it was all decided.
she's wrong; nothing is ever foreseen at all.
fork.reveal: Akiva sets them side by side: all is foreseen, and permission is given. He doesn't let either cancel the other.

original.note: Hebrew: permission is given, Akiva's half-line on freedom.

trapdoor: what you thought: fate or free will, pick one.
what it means: Akiva holds both, all foreseen and freedom given, and says the judging leans toward goodness.
what a scholar hears: hakol tzafui veharshut netunah in Avot 3:15, and Maimonides on why God's knowing doesn't cancel our choosing (Hilchot Teshuvah 5).

recall: loved, and dearer for being told

chat.says: told saba maybe i was just MEANT to be understudy. he laughed and said 'akiva disagrees.' does he??
options: half. Akiva says all is foreseen and freedom is given; how you play the part is yours.
yes. if it's all foreseen, trying harder can't change anything anyway.
no. Akiva says nothing is foreseen, so the cast list was pure chance.
chat.meaning: Hakol tzafui, veharshut netunah: all is foreseen, and freedom is given. Akiva keeps both, and the deeds still count.

Akiva.meaning: a rabbi whose sayings fill part of Avot chapter three

Maimonides.meaning: a medieval Jewish legal scholar and philosopher

sources.ref: Maimonides, Mishneh Torah, Hilchot Teshuvah 5:3 and 5:5

notes: v3 senses shape: tape marks on a stage floor carry the idea; the practice is one slow chosen movement.

Avot 3:15 has a textual variant: most printed texts read 'all according to the abundance of deeds' (vehakol lefi rov hama'aseh); some manuscripts read 'and not according to the deeds'. The script says 'all according to the weight of deeds' without comment. A scholar should confirm.
Maimonides: free choice as a great principle and pillar of Torah (Teshuvah 5:3); God's knowledge unlike ours (5:5). Paraphrased. Confirm.
Saba appears this week (in the chat). Practice kind: a body movement.
Noa storyline (the spring musical, days 1443–1456), day 4: at Shabbat dinner Noa tells Saba David she was maybe 'meant' to be the understudy; he laughs and says Akiva would disagree.
